name: DROP companion: California data-broker deletion verification report
buyer: Privacy-conscious California residents, especially those who work with the public (streamers, agents, landlords)
pain: Paid removal services are recurring and opaque. DROP now offers a free request channel, but users have no dated verification that their data actually disappeared from people-search sites.
wedge: Do not compete on removal. Walk a user through the DROP submission, re-check major people-search sites about 45 days later, and produce a dated listed/not-listed report.

scan1Edge.entrant_basis: A one-time fee of $15-$25 for a guided DROP submission and a re-check report, compared with DeleteMe's $129/year. The removal itself is free via DROP, so the entrant sells only guidance and verification.
scan1Edge.falsifier: If consumers will not pay for a free government service plus a verification report, or if people-search sites are not covered by registered brokers, there is no revenue.
scan1Edge.unit: USD in first year for removal verification

unitEconomicsNoted.notes: Model: one-time $15-$25 fee. Re-check scrapers break often. Handling personal data adds liability and legal review cost.

majorUncertainty: Whether anyone will pay a fee for a free government process, and whether an anonymous founder can earn the trust needed to handle personal data.
unknowns: Which people-search sites are registered brokers covered by DROP
Rules for authorized agents outside California
Willingness to pay for verification reports (no direct evidence)
Number of consumers using DROP (one vendor claims 325,000 requests, but this is not in the excerpts)
regulatoryOrPlatformDependency: Depends on California's DROP and the Delete Act. Rules for authorized agents in other states are unverified. Handling sensitive personal data as an anonymous founder is a trust and liability problem.
